incident-bot: PAGING: SLA_BREACH tenant=OrbitSoft service=api-inference check=orbitsoft_latency_p99 value=3.8s threshold=3.0s alert_id=alerts/ab12cd first_seen=1912345678
Alex K: Oncall here, investigating. Getting a bunch of pages from that tenant-specific latency check. p50/p90 look fine, p99 is spiking.
Alex K: Logs show a lot of long tail on the worker queue times. Could be background batch jobs from OrbitSoft. Not sure yet if it's customer-facing.
Maria Chen: looking at traces — many requests are internally queued for >1.5s before hitting GPU. There are also a handful of 502 timeouts from the proxy.
Maria Chen: snippet from the proxy logs:
```
2026-02-27T14:22:11Z orbitsoft-req-id=xx123 route=/v1/generate status=502 backend_wait=1800ms
2026-02-27T14:22:12Z orbitsoft-req-id=yy456 route=/v1/embeddings status=200 backend_wait=3200ms
```
Alex K: That backend_wait sequence is the cause of high p99. If these are long-running batch requests hitting the same tenant, they flood the worker queue and push up percentiles for all that tenant.
Sam - Support: I pinged OrbitSoft via the support channel (CS-5678). They say they launched a bulk migration job ~14:15 UTC and are seeing some timeouts. They also reported increased retries.
Tony (ops): Is this customer-visible SLA breach? If they're retrying and seeing failures in production, we need to treat as impact.
Alex K: I think partial customer impact. Some interactive requests are timing out (small fraction). But most production requests are okay. This is noisy: the tenant check is paging every minute.
Alex K: Short-term mitigation: silence the noisy per-tenant paging but keep it as a WARNING in the console; set a suppression that converts to an alert only if sustained for 5m OR error_rate > 5% AND error_count > 100.
Maria Chen: Agreed. We should not drop visibility, just avoid paging for a bursty background job. Also add an annotation suggesting 'possible batch job' when tenant tag present.
Alex K: I'm going to apply a temporary mute on alerts/ab12cd for 30m while we confirm customer impact. If impact increases, unmute and escalate.
Alex K: /incident mute alerts/ab12cd until +30m reason="noisy batch job from OrbitSoft, monitoring"
incident-bot: alerts/ab12cd muted until 30m by Alex K (reason: noisy batch job from OrbitSoft)
Jules - PM: FYI, OrbitSoft is a top-tier customer on a committed plan. We should document actions and follow up with them after.
Emma SRE: Will take ownership for the post-incident follow-up. Action items I will track: create a tenant-specific dashboard, add alert rule tweaks to the alerting repo, and open a runbook PR to classify "batch-induced latency".
Alex K: Here's a proposed alert rule change (example):
```
alert: TenantLatencyHigh
expr: |
  max_over_time(latency_p99{tenant="$tenant"}[5m]) > 3.0
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: warning
  tenant: "$tenant"
annotations:
  summary: "p99 latency high for tenant={{ $labels.tenant }}"
  runbook: "https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENGINF-1234"
  customer-impact: "conditional"
```
Alex K: And only escalate to page when both conditions met: for >=10m OR (error_rate > 0.05 and error_count > 100)
Maria Chen: Grafana query to visualize batch noise by request type:
```
sum by (tenant, request_type) (rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant="OrbitSoft"}[1m]))
```
Tony (ops): We should tag the check as `noisy: true` for tenant OrbitSoft and create a dashboard panel that surfaces long tail queue_time and backend_wait.
Sam - Support: I've updated the customer ticket: CS-5678 with our mitigation steps and asked OrbitSoft to pause the migration job if they can.
Jules - PM: Please make sure billing/comms are looped for any SLA exposure.
Emma SRE: I'll open ENGINF-1234 and assign tasks: dashboard (Emma), alert rule PR (Alex), runbook update (Emma), outreach summary (Sam).
Alex K: PRing the temporary alert tweak now, will include justification and metrics.
Alex K: Unmuting requirement: unmute earlier if error_rate goes above 5% for 2 consecutive 1m windows. I'll keep an eye on it.
incident-bot: alerts/ab12cd unmute scheduled at 1912347458 (or manually by owner)
Maria Chen: Quick note for postmortem: add a section on "tenant-specific thresholds" and recommend adding per-tenant burst protection (rate-limiting background jobs).
Emma SRE: Handoff — I'm taking the rest of the shift. I'll monitor for the next 3 hours and follow up with a runbook PR by EOD PST.
Alex K: Thanks all, standing down from active pages. Marking this thread as action_required.
Emma SRE: Acknowledged, taking over :white_check_mark:
